Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR enables PostgreSQL-backed CLI and Doctor operations while retaining Gateway execution restrictions and recovery ownership. **Example:** Run `openclaw models status --json` with PostgreSQL configured. - **Before:** Credential inspection can encounter the Gateway main-thread guard or read the local SQLite anchor. - **After:** The CLI selects PostgreSQL before inspection and uses the appropriate credential readers. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful CLI boundary evidence supports the approach, but the verified startup defect and unresolved upgrade compatibility prevent readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Real behavior proof is not required for maintainer- or bot-authored pull requests. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** PostgreSQL users cannot reliably run offline CLI and Doctor commands without execution refusals or incorrect SQLite state access. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction restores documented database ownership without adding public configuration or schemas. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** This maintainer-authored PR addresses a real PostgreSQL CLI failure, but a focused interactive-startup correction remains necessary. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `29a60c022ca97ab3774d83b96c83d55cbb825de3` ## Before merge - [ ] **Select configured storage before interactive setup reads state (P1)** - Interactive `onboard`, `setup --wizard` and `crestodian` receive the Gateway process role, so this branch maps them to the Gateway exclusion and returns without selecting storage. These routes have no equivalent final-target admission before their initial state reads: setup skips config preflight, while onboard uses its non-Gateway branch. Configuration/plugin inspection and the wizard's auth readers therefore use the default SQLite path against a PostgreSQL installation, potentially refusing the anchor or hiding persisted credentials. Prepare the configured engine before that work while retaining the Gateway role. This corroborates the existing Codex discussion. It is a late finding: the relevant classification and callers were unchanged at the previous reviewed head and should have been caught then. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P1] Select configured storage before interactive setup reads state — `src/cli/database-engine-selection.ts:105-107` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The recorded matrix excludes interactive PostgreSQL setup, and no latest-stable upgrade run demonstrates preserved settings, credentials and session data.
Agent review details ### How this fits together CLI startup resolves the command, configuration and storage target before dispatching to command owners; those owners read or mutate PostgreSQL state while local files retain identity anchors. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[CLI entry] --> B[Immutable process role] B --> C[Command and target selection] C --> D[Offline command owner] C --> E[Gateway admission owner] D --> F[PostgreSQL state] E --> F F --> G[Local identity anchors] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Prepare configured storage before interactive setup reads state, while preserving the Gateway process role and existing admission boundaries. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source tracing establishes the interactive selection failure; no target code or tests were executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Central selection and existing async readers fit the problem, but process-role classification must not imply that every Gateway-capable command already has a storage admission owner. Full review comments: - [P1] Select configured storage before interactive setup reads state — `src/cli/database-engine-selection.ts:105-107` Interactive `onboard`, `setup --wizard` and `crestodian` receive the Gateway process role, so this branch maps them to the Gateway exclusion and returns without selecting storage. These routes have no equivalent final-target admission before their initial state reads: setup skips config preflight, while onboard uses its non-Gateway branch. Configuration/plugin inspection and the wizard's auth readers therefore use the default SQLite path against a PostgreSQL installation, potentially refusing the anchor or hiding persisted credentials. Prepare the configured engine before that work while retaining the Gateway role. This corroborates the existing Codex discussion. It is a late finding: the relevant classification and callers were unchanged at the previous reviewed head and should have been caught then.
